The '''1993–94 Scottish Premier Division''' season began on 7 August 1993 and was the last season of the twelve-team league, with three teams relegated to make way for the ten-team league the following season. It was also the final season with the rule of awarding [[Three points for a win|two points for a win]], with three points given from then on.

==Overview==
The 1993–94 Scottish Premier Division season ended in success for [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who won the title by three points from nearest rivals [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] to clinch six titles in a row.<ref>[https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/shadows-1994-rangers-fans-remember-25027978 The shadows of 1994 as Rangers fans remember the 50 per cent rule that saw off Celtic], Daily Record, 20 September 2021</ref> [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] were relegated to the [[Scottish Football League First Division|First Division]] after finishing in the bottom three positions. As champions, Rangers qualified for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] while Aberdeen were joined by third-placed [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in qualifying for the [[UEFA Cup]]. Sixth-placed [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] qualified for the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] after winning the [[Scottish Cup]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/scot94.html|title=Scottish Premier Division 1993/94|access-date=2008-10-03| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080922033632/http://www.rsssf.com/tabless/scot94.html| archive-date= 22 September 2008 |website=[[RSSSF]]| url-status= live}}</ref>
